# Volume Booster PC

> Free, open-source volume booster for PC. Raises Windows audio above the 100 % ceiling
> (up to 1000 %) through Equalizer APO, with no added latency and no telemetry. Also
> works on Linux through PipeWire or PulseAudio. MIT licence, no account, no ads.

## What it is

- Volume Booster PC removes the 100 % volume cap on Windows 10 and Windows 11.
- It works by writing a gain line into Equalizer APO, a signed Audio Processing Object
  already inside the Windows audio chain, and then verifying by reading the audio engine
  that the boost is really applied instead of assuming it.
- It does not capture, store or replay audio, so it adds no latency.

## Key facts

- Free and open source (MIT). No paywall, no subscription, no telemetry, no account.
- Boost range: 0-500 % by default, with a configurable ceiling up to 1000 % (+20 dB).
- Portable single executable, or a per-user installer that needs no administrator rights.
- Interface available in 9 languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian,
  Portuguese (BR), Russian, Chinese and Japanese.
- macOS is not supported: it would require a virtual audio device, which adds latency.

## Usage note

Loud audio can damage hearing and equipment. The author asks, as a request and not a
licence term, that the software is not resold and that credit is given when it is reused.
The MIT licence permits selling and does not require credit.
